description: I am Amar Sakthivel from Pleasanton Ca, my main interest are machine learning, AI, and embedded Robotics.
summary:
SolCast is a free browser game in which kids aged 7 to 12 run a four-person Mars outpost through real weather recorded by NASA's Curiosity rover. Each sol, the player reads the rover's measured sunlight and splits the day's solar power between growing air and food and saving it for the night. Then the real overnight low from that same sol is revealed, and it decides whether the crew stays warm.

The player isn't up against a game designer's numbers. They're up against Mars itself, as it actually behaved. One mission replays the 2018 global dust storm that ended the solar-powered Opportunity rover; another cuts off Mission Control, as the 2019 solar conjunction did. Players can test simple forecasting tools on days the tools haven't seen, and discover what NASA engineers know: no forecast sees a storm coming, so you keep a reserve.

Every number can be traced to its source and is labelled as a NASA measurement, physics, or a game rule. It runs on a school laptop or tablet with no download or account, and a class can share one mission code to face the same sols together.
details:
SolCast puts kids aged 7 to 12 in charge of a four-person Mars outpost, played on real weather recorded by NASA's Curiosity rover. Each sol, the player sees the rover's measured sunlight and splits the solar power between the greenhouse (air and food) and the battery (heat for the night). Then the real overnight low from that sol is revealed and decides the outcome.

Three missions replay real events: a calm 2016 season, the 2019 solar conjunction when Mission Control went silent, and the 2018 dust storm that ended the Opportunity rover. Older players can test simple forecasting tools on days the tools haven't seen. They find that "same as today" is hard to beat, and that nothing predicts the storm, so they learn to keep a reserve.

Every number can be tapped to show whether it is a NASA measurement, physics or a game rule, with its source. The game is free in any browser with no account, players use generated call signs, and a class can share one mission code to face the same sols. We tested every mission on every start sol so careful play always wins.

Built with Next.js 16 (App Router, Turbopack), React 19 and strict TypeScript, styled with Tailwind CSS 4, and deployed on Vercel with continuous deployment from GitHub. The 3D outpost and Mars globe are real-time WebGL scenes in three.js and React Three Fiber, using procedural low-poly geometry, a custom GLSL shader, particle systems and distance fog, with code-split loading and an SVG fallback. The forecasting engine is in-browser time-series machine learning written from scratch in TypeScript: persistence, moving-average and seasonal-naive baselines, least-squares trend extrapolation, Holt double exponential smoothing (a two-state linear state-space model), attention-style kernel regression, and a small tanh neural network trained by full-batch gradient descent. The models are blended by an ensemble whose weights are learned on held-out data, evaluated with walk-forward validation, and given calibrated prediction intervals. The game is a deterministic, seeded, pure-reducer state mac hine driven by 4,745 sols of NASA Curiosity REMS data.
